body.x: DIGITIMES, a Taiwanese technology and industry outlet, named LVIS Korea Co., Ltd., OPTOELEC Co., Ltd. and KAR Co., Ltd. its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

DIGITIMES is a Taiwanese technology news and research outlet covering semiconductors, ICT, the electronics industry and global technology supply chains. It is strong at analyzing not only a technology's performance but also its potential use in industrial ecosystems, market scalability and potential for cooperation with global companies.

DIGITIMES joined this year as a global media partner, and Sherri Wang, research editor, covered the show. In a pre-event interview, Wang said she would focus on the growth potential of the physical AI and robotics ecosystem and on whether new technologies can be applied at actual industrial sites and how competitive they can be in global supply chains.

The three companies DIGITIMES chose show how technology can be used in different fields: AI-based neuro-medical software, wafer-level optics, and integrated engineering for autonomous driving and future mobility.
LVIS Korea's NeuroMatch Supports EEG Analysis and Neurological Diagnosis With AI

LVIS Korea Co., Ltd. is a medical technology company that uses AI to analyze brain neural network data and support doctors' EEG reading and clinical work in treating neurological disease. Its flagship solution, NeuroMatch®, is a software platform for analyzing and reviewing electroencephalography (EEG) data, designed to let doctors review complex EEG recordings more efficiently and improve clinical workflow.

NeuroMatch supports AI-based spike and seizure detection, EEG data visualization, signal review and remote collaboration among medical staff. Its core purpose is to help doctors review large volumes of EEG data efficiently and identify clinically meaningful signals, which reduces the burden of EEG reading and lets them check the information needed for neurological diagnosis more systematically.

In treating neurological disease, reading the complex signals in EEG data accurately and efficiently is important. With software that links AI analysis to doctors' clinical judgment, LVIS Korea supports digital transformation and more efficient clinical work in neuro-medicine.
OPTOELEC Targets Future Mobility and Photonics With Ultra-Precise Wafer-Level Optics

OPTOELEC Co., Ltd. is a wafer-level optics (WLO) specialist that applies precision semiconductor process technology to optics. It supports optical component development and manufacturing with technology that links ultra-precise micro lens array design, wafer-level molding, micro-packaging and inspection.

Its main business is automotive electrical optics for future mobility. In materials made public for DIFA 2026, it presented WLO-based intelligent headlamp optics, road-projection lighting and 3D floating light modules for vehicles. With ultra-slim, lightweight designs and precise light control, it focuses on delivering a range of lighting functions within the limited space of a vehicle and widening the design and functions of future cars.

OPTOELEC also offers a WLO-based custom photonics foundry service. It designs and manufactures micro-optical structures to customers' optical requirements, supporting work from prototype development to linkage with mass production. The company is also extending its technology into next-generation optical applications such as silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (CPO).

As AI data processing and high-speed communication advance, photonics, which combines semiconductors and optics, is gaining importance. The ability to design and reliably manufacture ultra-precise optical components, from vehicle lighting and optical sensors to next-generation optical communication and computing infrastructure, can support technological progress across industries. OPTOELEC is expanding its business in future mobility and next-generation optics on its semiconductor process-based WLO technology and integrated manufacturing capability.
KAR Integrates Custom Mobility and Autonomous Vehicle Technology

KAR Co., Ltd. provides integrated engineering solutions for autonomous driving and eco-friendly future mobility based on mechatronics design, embedded control systems and vehicle electrical integration technology. It connects the technologies needed for vehicle development, from vehicle design and conversion to sensor and computing system integration, power and communication architecture design, vehicle control interface building, and on-road evaluation and verification.

The main product it presented at the show, the go-kart platform, is an on-road R&D platform for autonomous driving research and education and algorithm development and verification. It integrates autonomous driving sensors and computing systems so technology can be tested and verified in a real vehicle environment. Because algorithms developed in the lab can be applied to a real vehicle to confirm how they operate, the platform is aimed at research institutes and autonomous driving technology developers.

KAR stresses its ability to integrate vehicle structure, electrical systems and control technology to fit a customer's driving purpose and environment, going beyond supplying vehicles or parts. Drawing on experience in building autonomous vehicles and system integration projects in Korea and overseas, it works in custom mobility development and on-road verification. It also drew attention by presenting tourist electric mobility that operates at Ulsan Grand Park and Taehwagang National Garden.

For autonomous driving and eco-friendly mobility to expand onto real roads and public spaces, vehicle hardware, electrical systems, sensors and control technology have to connect with software. KAR responds to a range of mobility development needs with engineering capability that runs from vehicle design to system integration and on-road verification.
Core Technology for the Physical AI Era

In its FIX 2026 pre-event interview, DIGITIMES pointed to the growth potential of the physical AI and robotics ecosystem and the supply chain strength of Korean companies. It looked at technology capability and potential industrial use together, from AI software to core optical components and autonomous driving system integration.

The companies chosen for the top three belong to different fields, but each turns specialized technology into a solution that can be applied in industry. They show that progress in physical AI and robotics is not limited to finished robots: the AI software, precision components and system integration technology that make them possible matter as well. The selection offers a way to gauge the global market potential of Korean companies through this technology base and the links between industries.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including DIGITIMES. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners took part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and covered firsthand news from innovative companies set to lead Korea's future industries, introducing it to readers around the world.
